A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same NoPain research and provide readable text, equations, algorithms, tables and figures. All 11 pages of each were inspected; both end with references and neither contains an appendix.

before.justification: Sections 4.2-4.4 report original attack-transferability experiments, defense evaluations, qualitative examples and hyperparameter studies in Tables 1-2 and Figures 3-4.

after.justification: v4 retains the work's original experimental results in Tables 1-2 and Figures 3-4, including transferability, defense and sensitivity evaluations.

M1.justification: The encoding, OT hyperplane solver, singular-boundary selection, feature interpolation and decoding procedures are unchanged. Algorithms 1-2 and the PointFlow and Point-Diffusion variants are retained.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate point-cloud classification attacks on ModelNet40 and ShapeNetPart, with the same transferability and defense scenarios. No dataset, task or domain is added or removed.

E2.justification: Tables 1-2 retain the same five attack comparators: AdvPC, AOF, SI-Adv, SS-attack and HiT-ADV. The newly cited OT-Net is not evaluated as a comparator.

E3.justification: The dataset splits, PointNet++ surrogate for baseline attacks, target classifiers, ASR/CD/time metrics and experimental procedures are unchanged. The stated hyperparameters, including K = 11 and the dataset-specific thresholds of 1.6 and 0.9, also match.

E4.justification: Both retain the same four defense evaluations, qualitative examples in Figure 3, and neighbor-count and threshold sensitivity studies in Figure 4. No ablation, robustness test or supplementary analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, experimental seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests or uncertainty bars. Statistical reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1-2 match, including NoPain-PD's 100% ASR on ModelNet40 against PointNet. Figures 3-4 retain the same adversarial examples and sensitivity curves, and the reported findings are unchanged.

T1.justification: The semi-discrete OT formulation, Brenier potential, height-vector optimization and boundary/interpolation definitions in Equations 1-8 are unchanged. No mathematical assumption, derivation or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions and conclusion retain the same claims about classifier-free attacks using OT singular boundaries, transferability, efficiency and robustness against defenses.

C2.justification: The explanations linking singular-boundary mode mixing and avoidance of classifier-specific optimization to transferability remain unchanged. Both also retain the qualification that explicitly calculating discrete singular boundaries can be intractable; no substantive limitation or applicability boundary is added.

D1.justification: v1 promises a future public source-code release; v4's abstract supplies a repository link and states that code and a model are available. This adds concrete access information, while implementation descriptions, hardware and hyperparameters remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v4 adds Li et al.'s OT-Net: A reusable neural optimal transport solver as reference 31 in the introduction's OT discussion. Descriptions of several white-box attacks are shortened, but the other cited works and the paper's research positioning are retained.

P1.justification: v4 condenses the white-box related-work discussion, makes a small abstract grammar correction, updates affiliations and corresponding-author information, and adds acknowledgments. Section order and the main scientific narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: Spacing around Figure 2 is tightened, and text reflow brings the conclusion entirely onto page 8 instead of continuing onto page 9. The same four figures, two result tables and two algorithm boxes remain, with unchanged plotted content, axes, legends and table organization.

improvement.justification: The abstract's concrete code/model access information modestly improves reproducibility documentation over v1's future-release promise. Shortened related work loses some descriptive detail, but the method, mathematical exposition, experimental evidence and conclusions remain intact. The supported overall gain is limited.
